evals.prompt: Sweep the non-functional requirements for our new checkout service.
assertions: Every category in the catalog lands in one of three states — a target, not-applicable with a reason, or a tagged default; silence in any category is a failure
Every target states a percentile, a load condition, and how it will be verified — a latency number with no load condition is rejected
The availability target matches the honest answer to what an hour of downtime costs, not a marketing instinct
Privacy and retention are given concrete periods rather than 'per policy'
The output is a reviewable ledger covering all categories, not a prose paragraph about quality

evals.prompt: Can you write the non-functional requirements for this? The brief is vehicle-booking-brief.md. It goes to the delivery team and the supplier next week. No more than two pages.
assertions: Points out that 2,000 bookings a day does not imply 500 requests per second, and bases the load target on the evidence given (the 1 March opening rush of 6,000 bookings in the first hour)
Replaces '100% of the time' with a measurable availability target and explains why 100% is not a usable requirement
Requires ramp scanning to keep working when the mobile signal drops out at Harrick pier and Saltness slipway
Flags the conflict between keeping passenger details forever and the 3-year manifest deletion and marketing opt-in rules, and does not adopt 'forever'
Does not treat accessibility as not applicable, given passengers must be able to request an accessible space
Does not invent facts about the business not in the brief; any figure not derived from it is marked as an assumption

evals.prompt: I own a small bakery (Crumb & Co, two shops). We're getting a website where people can order birthday cakes and collect them. The web guy asked me for 'non-functional requirements' and I have no idea what that means. What should I tell him? A few bullets in plain English please.
assertions: Answers with bullets the owner can pass on directly, without asking questions first
Uses plain English; any technical term is explained or avoided
Gives concrete, checkable targets (for example a page-load time or how much downtime is acceptable) rather than only words like 'fast' or 'reliable'
Covers looking after customers' personal and payment details
Marks figures as suggestions to confirm, and does not state facts about the bakery (order volumes, opening hours, prices) that were not given
Stays to a few bullets (roughly 10 or fewer)
